_how: Recipe for shorts.build (video-machine). 13 clips (fire-first dropped: only 18 s) from Jason Harris (All About Septic Services Inc.) guest episode, take 135607 (Zoom HD 1280x720, speaker view, no upscale, lip-synced: Jason 40 ms earlier). keep = inclusive word-index ranges; per-clip fixes are the episode fixes inside the clip (Ryan Gascon in wastewater-plant). Posting plan: release week from 2026-12-23, every clip to YouTube + TikTok, two a day at noon and 5 PM CT, skipping Christmas Day (12-25), through 12-30; the five strongest (cheapest, wastewater-plant, dont-wear-it, terralift, flood) also to Instagram and Facebook at noon on weekdays (12-23, 12-24, 12-28, 12-29, 12-30). {jason} tags Jason Harris, {aas} tags All About Septic Services; no handles or Facebook page id yet (see final message), the full episode linked ({episode}) everywhere but Facebook.
cover_with: with Jason Harris of All About Septic Services

clips.title:
Don't be the *cheapest*
septic company in town

youtube.title: Why the cheapest septic company in town is the one losing money

captions.facebook:
A septic owner is buried in calls, and his trucks are falling apart. Another septic company calls a meeting and tells him to stop being the cheapest. {jason} of {aas} says he thought he would lose all his customers, so the advice sat in his head for two years. Then he got tired of working for nothing and raised his prices. He went from one pump truck to eleven.

#septic

youtube.title: He started a septic company with shoe polish on a pickup truck

clips.title:
I built my own septic
*wastewater plant* from scratch

youtube.title: A septic owner built his own wastewater treatment plant from scratch

captions.facebook:
More septic calls than you can handle sounds like a good problem, until you ask where all that waste is going. {jason} of {aas} ran into it in Highlands County. The local dump site told him to come first thing in the morning because they closed by 10. So he jumped in knee-deep and built his own wastewater treatment plant from scratch, with advice from his friend Ryan Gascon.

#septic

clips.title:
Raise your septic prices and
*lose* the wrong customers

youtube.title: Raise your septic prices and lose the wrong customers

captions.facebook:
You raise your prices, and the customers you were most afraid of losing do exactly what you feared. {jason} of {aas} says he thought, man, I'm going to lose so many customers, and he did. But he says those weren't the customers he wanted. They were the ones always using him, and when he raised his rate they said they'd just go to the next guy. His take: someone who does that is not a good customer, and you have to want your company to be an A-rated company.

#septic

clips.title:
Just because we're in septic

youtube.title: Just because you are in the septic business does not mean you wear it

captions.facebook:
Why is it so hard to find people who will drive a pump truck? {jason} of {aas} says it begins with education. Everybody thinks you will get covered in poop. He tells them: see how I come to work? This is how I leave work. Just because we are in the septic business does not mean we need to wear it.

#septic

clips.title:
My dad said I'd never
*amount* to anything

youtube.title: A septic owner who dropped out in 9th grade and kept learning

captions.facebook:
Imagine hearing from your own dad that you're never going to amount to anything. {jason} of {aas} dropped out of high school in 9th grade and got his GED, and his dad, who worked in septic too, told him exactly that. Jason says that's what pushes him, and he likes to be pushed. His dad started three separate septic companies over the years, one of them with a business partner. Jason's take on that one: do not recommend business partners.

#septic

clips.title:
We charged *normal rates*
during the flood

youtube.title: Septic company kept normal rates during a flood and served 300 customers

captions.facebook:
When the neighborhoods flood, the calls come in left and right. A lot of septic companies called it an emergency and charged emergency rates. {jason} of {aas} did the opposite. His crews did around 300 customers at the same rate as any Monday through Friday, and out of all of them, not one broken tank and not one that popped out of the ground.

#septic
